subject: MAP: Performance acceptance & throughput economics (Q4 close plan)

Subject: MAP: Performance acceptance & throughput economics (Q4 close plan)

Alex / Procurement team —

Following our call this morning, attached is the updated MAP section for performance acceptance criteria and the benchmarking plan we discussed. High level ask: we want to validate sustained throughput and unit economics under your peak billing workload before we finalize the committed capacity in the contract. Key items included:

- Acceptance targets (must pass to sign):
  - TTFT (time-to-first-token) <= 160ms at p50 for conversational requests
  - Sustained throughput: >= 1,200 tokens/sec (aggregate) at target concurrency of 32
  - Sustained QPS: >= 45 QPS for the 1.5K-token average request size profile
  - 99.9% of requests under 850ms tail latency at concurrency <= 64 for the first-phase model
- Evaluation plan: 3-run sweep across quantization and batching profiles, continuous KV cache enabled for prefix-heavy flows
- Metrics we will publish: tokens/sec, sustained QPS, TTFT, p50/p95/p99 latency, GPU utilization, and cost-per-1M-tokens (hosted vs dedicated)
- Timeline (MAP milestones):
  - Bench setup & script handoff: 11/22
  - Customer test window: 11/24 - 11/27
  - Results delivery & findings review: 11/27 - 11/29
  - Sign/commit decision: targeted 12/03 (end of Q4 close window)

Attachments: redwood-bench-plan-v2.pdf (plan + config), bench-template.csv. Please confirm the test window and reply with the primary test key (example workload ID) you want us to run against.

Thanks —
Markus
Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

We'll provide the workload ID and a sanitized sample dataset by EOD 11/24. Also looping in procurement to confirm legal/compliance checkpoints for the Dedicated SLA.

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.k@redwood.com>

Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.o@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-27T14:08:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MAP: Performance acceptance & throughput economics (Q4 close plan)

Alex — thanks for the questions and for the sample workload. We ran the customer test window (11/24–11/26) against two deployment profiles: Hosted (multi-tenant, standard cluster) and Dedicated (4x A100-equivalent GPUs, optimized runtime). Below is a concise results summary — full raw results attached (finledger-bench-raw-20261127.csv).

Benchmark summary (median of 3 runs, 1.5k avg request tokens):
- Hosted profile:
  - Aggregate sustained tokens/sec: 1,060 tokens/sec
  - Sustained QPS (avg request 1.5k tokens): ~0.71 QPS per concurrent client; aggregate sustained QPS: 36 QPS
  - TTFT p50: 180 ms; p95: 430 ms
  - p99 tail latency: 1,200 ms (observed spikes under concurrency >48)
  - GPU utilization (avg): 62%
  - Unit economics: estimated cost per 1M tokens = $0.92 (hosted list) — projected monthly cost at 2M tokens/day: ~$55k/month

- Dedicated (4x pod, optimized kernels + quantization):
  - Aggregate sustained tokens/sec: 1,650 tokens/sec
  - Sustained QPS: 48 QPS (measured at concurrency 32)
  - TTFT p50: 145 ms; p95: 290 ms
  - p99 tail latency: 680 ms
  - GPU utilization (avg): 88% (good headroom for burst)
  - Unit economics: amortized cost per 1M tokens with reserved capacity assumptions = $0.18 — projected monthly cost at 2M tokens/day: ~$10.8k/month (note: committed pricing and infra ops add-ons affect final contract math)

Concurrency vs behavior notes (Dedicated):
- Concurrency 1–8: near linear latency scaling, TTFT unchanged
- Concurrency 16–32: throughput increases toward sustained peak; p95 under 320 ms
- Concurrency 64: throughput plateaued; increased p99 events likely due to scheduling contention — recommend a soft concurrency cap at 48 for peak SLAs or additional pod capacity for headroom.

Acceptance checklist (based on agreed targets):
- TTFT p50 <= 160 ms: Hosted = FAIL, Dedicated = PASS
- Sustained throughput >= 1,200 tokens/sec: Hosted = FAIL, Dedicated = PASS
- Sustained QPS >= 45 QPS: Hosted = FAIL, Dedicated = PASS
- 99.9% < 850 ms at concurrency <= 64: Hosted = FAIL (p99 spikes), Dedicated = PARTIAL (p99 ~680 ms, passes)

Recommended path to close:
1) Move to Dedicated reserved capacity (4x) with option to scale to 6x on 30-day notice — this meets MAP acceptance and provides the unit-econ delta procurement needs.
2) Add a short canary period (7 days) in production traffic routing with automatic fallback to Hosted for anomalies.
3) Finalize committed term to lock in the $0.18/1M token amortized price and SLAs (we'll provide final contract language to procurement).

I've attached the raw CSV and the config used. Happy to run any additional scenarios (e.g., lower quantization vs mixed precision).

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Performance Lead, Redwood Inference

Alex / Procurement —

Thanks for reviewing the results. Short summary and proposed next steps to keep us inside the Q4 close window:

- Executive summary: Dedicated 4x meets MAP acceptance across throughput and latency, and yields ~5x better unit economics at scale vs Hosted for your 2M-tokens/day profile. Hosted is a quick-start but does not meet the acceptance bar for this MAP.

Proposed immediate actions (for sign-off):
- Procurement to confirm: commit to 12-month Dedicated with 4x capacity + 30% burst option OR sign 24-month to secure additional discount (we can model both RH scenarios).
- Legal: we'll share a short SLA amendment for the Dedicated tier (turnaround 48 hours).
- Ops/CS: plan a 7-day canary starting after contract countersign (we will supply routing config & rollback playbook).

If procurement confirms commitment by COB 12/03 we can schedule legal and start the canary week of 12/07 so the production swing is within your internal launch cadence.

Please reply with procurement's preferred commitment term (12m / 24m) and we'll table the contract numbers.

Best —
